user.description:
A **data source** holds the timetable of one transport network. **Sensors** read from it: as many as you like, on the same source.

[documentation]({docu_menu_options})

menu_options.source: Add a data source: the GTFS file of a transport network

user_empty.description:
You have no data source yet. Add one first: it holds the timetable of a transport network, and every sensor reads from it.

[documentation]({docu_menu_options})

start_end.description:
Which transport network should this sensor read?

[documentation]({docu_select_source})

data_description.file: Sources already present in your `gtfs2` folder. Add one first if the list is empty.

local_stops.description:
Every departure, all routes, around one location.

[documentation]({docu_local_stops})

data_description.file: Sources already present in your `gtfs2` folder.
data_description.device_tracker_id: The stops are looked up around this person or zone, and follow them when they move.

source.description:
Where should the transport data come from?

[documentation]({docu_extracting})

data.url: Web address of the GTFS file

source_url.description:
Home Assistant will download the file and unpack it into a local database.

[documentation]({docu_extracting})

data_description.url: The `.zip` published by the transport network.
data_description.file: Your own name for this source. It identifies it later, and names the file on disk. Letters and digits, no spaces.
data_description.needs_api_key: Tick this if the provider gave you a key to download the file.

source_key.description:
The provider states these in its documentation.

[documentation]({docu_extracting})

data_description.api_key: The key itself, copied from the provider.
data_description.api_key_name: The word placed before your key. In the address: `?`**`apikey`**`=YOUR_KEY`. In a header: **`x-api-key`**`: YOUR_KEY`. It differs between providers (`apikey`, `api_key`, `app_key`, `Authorization`) and is case sensitive.
data_description.api_key_location: In the web address, or in the request header.

source_zip.description:
The file will be unpacked into a local database. A large network can take several minutes.

[documentation]({docu_extracting})

data_description.file: The `.zip` files found in your `gtfs2` folder.

data_description.agency: Pick one to shorten the route list on the next screen, or **ALL** to keep every route.

route.description:
Which line should this sensor follow?

[documentation]({docu_new_route})

data_description.route: **{routes}** of the **{routes_total}** lines in this source have timetables loaded. Lines a cleanup removed are still offered: choosing one brings it back, without touching the others.

route_reload.title: Line {route} has no timetable loaded
route_reload.description:
The timetables for this line were removed to save space. Bringing them back means unpacking the network file, which takes a few minutes.

It costs the same whether one line or ten come back, so the **{missing}** other missing lines are offered below.

Your other sensors keep working, and nothing you leave unticked comes back.

[documentation]({docu_new_route})

data.also_reload: Bring back at the same time

data_description.also_reload: Leave empty to bring back only this line.

route_reload_only.title: Line {route} has no timetable loaded
route_reload_only.description:
The timetables for this line were removed to save space. Bringing them back means unpacking the network file, which takes a few minutes.

Your other sensors keep working throughout, and no other line comes back.

[documentation]({docu_new_route})

data_description.direction: A sensor follows one direction. You can add a second sensor for the way back.

direction.description:
Which way should the sensor follow this line?

[documentation]({docu_new_route})

stops.description:
Which part of the line should the sensor watch?

[documentation]({docu_new_route})

data_description.origin: Departures are counted from here. The list follows the direction of travel; a number tells apart two platforms sharing a name.
data_description.destination: Used to keep only the trips that call at both stops, in this order. Leave it on the end of the line to see everything passing by.

data.name: Sensor name
data.include_tomorrow: Also show tomorrow's departures at the end of the day's service

data_description.name: Suggested from the line and the two stops. Shown on your dashboard.
data_description.include_tomorrow: Without this, the sensor is empty between the last departure of the day and the first of the next.
data_description.add_return: A second sensor for **{return_trip}**, the same line the other way.

sensor.description:
The sensor will show the next departures for **{trip}**.

[documentation]({docu_new_route})

data.include_tomorrow: Also show tomorrow's departures at the end of the day's service

stops_train.description:
The sensor will show the next trains between two stations.

[documentation]({docu_setup_train})

data_description.origin: Stations served by this route. A station appears once here, even when the feed splits it into several stops.
data_description.destination: Same list. Pick the one you travel to.
data_description.include_tomorrow: Without this, the sensor is empty between the last departure of the day and the first of the next.

sensor_train.description: The sensor will show the next trains for **{trip}**.

data_description.name: Suggested from the line and the stations, change it freely.
data_description.add_return: A second sensor for **{return_trip}**, the same journey the other way.

remove.description:
Deletes the source **and its database**. Sensors that read from it will stop working.

[documentation]({docu_menu_options})

data_description.file: The `.zip` and the database are both removed from `gtfs2`.

finished.title: Sensor created
finished.description:
**{name}** is ready and will appear on your dashboard.

Most networks need a few journeys: one line each way, or a couple of lines. Adding them now reuses the source you just picked.

[documentation]({docu_new_route})

optimise.title: Free up disk space
optimise.description:
The source **{file}** takes **{size}**. Most of it is timetables for lines no sensor reads.

**{kept}** line(s) kept, **{dropped}** removed.

Removing them and compacting what remains often divides the size by ten or more. A removed line can always be added back later.

This takes a few seconds.

[documentation]({docu_extracting})

source_rt.description:
Realtime is set up once per source: every sensor reading this source shares these feeds. Enter only the ones you want, **departures** is the only one that switches realtime on. You can also leave everything empty and add the feeds later, from this source's entry in the integration page.

[documentation]({docu_configuring_options})

data_description.trip_update_url:
The real delay on your sensor, instead of the timetable.
`https://example.org/gtfs/`**`trip-updates`**
data_description.vehicle_position_url:
Where the vehicles are, for a map card. Leave empty if you do not want it.
`https://example.org/gtfs/`**`vehicle-positions`**
data_description.alerts_url:
Disruption messages from the operator. Leave empty if you do not want it.
`https://example.org/gtfs/`**`service-alerts`**
data_description.needs_api_key: Tick this if the provider gave you a key to read these feeds.

source_rt_key.description:
The provider states these in its documentation.

[documentation]({docu_configuring_options})

data.accept: Also send Accept: application/x-protobuf (only applies when the key goes in the header)

data_description.api_key: The key itself, copied from the provider.
data_description.api_key_name: The word placed before your key. In the address: `?`**`apikey`**`=YOUR_KEY`. In a header: **`x-api-key`**`: YOUR_KEY`. It differs between providers (`apikey`, `api_key`, `app_key`, `Authorization`) and is case sensitive.
data_description.api_key_location: In the web address, or in the request header.
data_description.accept: Only applies when the key goes in the header.

error.stop_incorrect: No departure found between these two cities. Check the spelling against the operator's own, and that they are on the same line.
error.no_data_file: Could not download the file. Check the address, and that the source is reachable from Home Assistant. Some providers reject automated downloads.
error.no_zip_file: Data collection issue: ZIP file not in the correct folder
error.stops_out_of_order: The arrival stop comes before the departure stop on this line. The list follows the direction of travel: pick an arrival further down, or go back and choose the other direction.
error.no_trip_between: No trip on this line calls at both stops in this order. Pick another pair, or go back and take the other direction.
error.name_taken: A sensor already uses this name. Pick another one.
error.not_created: The sensor could not be created. Check the log, then try a different name.
error.reload_failed: That line could not be brought back. The datasource was left untouched; pick another line, or try again.

abort.files_deleted: Datasource deleted, this may affect existing routes
abort.stop_incorrect:
Start and/or End destination incorrect, 
 possibly no transport 'today' or not in same direction, 
 please check logs
abort.no_data_file: Data collection issue: URL incorrect or filename not in the correct folder
abort.no_stops: Data collection issue: probably no stops for the selected route
abort.no_zip_file: Data collection issue: ZIP file not existing in the correct folder, note that it is capital-sensitive
abort.stop_limit_reached:
Detected a high number of stops for this radius, 
possibly impacting system performance. 
 You can change the limit at your own risk before changing the radius.
abort.extracting: (Still) extracting data, this will take time [documentation]({docu_extracting})
abort.no_zip_in_folder: No .zip file found in {folder}. Place your GTFS zip file there, then start again.
abort.no_routes_with_trips: No route in this datasource has a timetable loaded. Run the update_gtfs service to reload it from the source.
abort.no_stops_read: Could not read the stops of this route. Check the logs: the datasource may be busy or being rebuilt.
abort.reload_failed: The line could not be brought back. The network file may be missing or unreadable; the datasource itself was left untouched.
abort.optimised: Disk space freed. The source now takes {size}.
abort.finished: Setup complete. You can add more journeys at any time from the integration page.
abort.unpacking:
{file} is being unpacked in the background. This takes several minutes, so there is nothing to wait for here.

A notification will tell you when the source is ready, and where to carry on. Do not restart Home Assistant before then, it would stop the job.

progress.extracting:
**You can close this window.**

A notification will tell you when {file} is ready: the unpacking carries on in the background.

Staying here lets you chain straight on to picking a line. **{size}** so far; on a large network this takes several minutes.

Do not restart Home Assistant before then, it would stop the job.
progress.importing:
**You can close this window.**

A notification will tell you when it is done: the {routes} line(s) from {file} carry on being brought back in the background.

Staying here lets you chain straight on to picking the stops. **{size}** unpacked so far; your other sensors keep working.

Do not restart Home Assistant before then, it would stop the job.

init.description:
Adjust how often this sensor refreshes and what it reports.

[documentation]({docu_configuring_options})

data.max_local_stops:
Limit #stops to avoid possible performance impact. 
Increase at your own risk
data.timerange: Checking for departures in future from 'now' (in minutes: between 15 and 120)
data.check_source_dates: experimental: avoid using new zip/source contain having no current information
data.radius: Radius to search for stops (in meters between 50 and 500)

data_description.refresh_interval: How often the timetable is re-read, in minutes.
data_description.local_stop_refresh_interval: How often the nearby stops are re-read, in minutes.
data_description.offset: Hide departures you could not catch: the walking time to the stop, in minutes.
data_description.timerange: How far ahead to look for departures, in minutes.
data_description.radius: How far around the person or zone to look for stops, in metres.
data_description.max_local_stops: Above this many stops the sensor gets slow. Raise it at your own risk.
data_description.source_timezone_correction: Only if the source publishes times in another timezone, in hours.
data_description.check_source_dates: Experimental: refuse a new file whose dates are all in the future.

real_time.description:
These feeds belong to the whole source: every sensor reading it uses them, within a minute, no restart needed. **departures** is the only one that switches realtime on. Empty a field to drop that feed, empty them all to remove realtime from this source.

data_description.alerts_url:

data_description.needs_api_key: Tick this if the provider gave you a key to read these feeds.

data_description.api_key_location: In the web address, or in the request header.

static_refresh.title: Static feed updates
static_refresh.description: What this source does about new versions of its timetable feed. **Notify** asks the host at the check time with one tiny request and says when a new version exists, so you or an automation decide when to install. **Install automatically** installs it right away. Sensors keep answering during an install; the switch to the new data happens in one go.

data_description.static_refresh_mode: Off changes nothing for this source.
data_description.static_check_time: One check per day, at this time. Prefilled with a slot of the source's own, so sources spread out.

update_gtfs_local_stops.name: Update GTFS local stops
update_gtfs_local_stops.description: e.g. for moving 'person', to be defined for each person / zone

entity_id.name: Entity that is connected to local stops
entity_id.description: The entity for which you setup local stops

extract_departures.name: Extract departures
extract_departures.description: Extracts all next departures from your entity up-until tomorrow day end

from_time.name: The time after which departures are collected
from_time.description:
The time after which you would like to receive the slots. 
 If left empty then all future slots will be extracted for today/tomorrow. 
 In yaml this has to be 24H format

extract_trip_stops.name: Extract the stops of a trip
extract_trip_stops.description: Returns the ordered stops of the trip a sensor is currently following.

entity_id.name: Sensor
entity_id.description: The start/end sensor to read the current trip from

set_include_tomorrow.name: Show tomorrow's departures
set_include_tomorrow.description: Turns tomorrow's departures on or off on existing sensors, without recreating them.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: On to keep showing departures once the day's service is over

entry_id.name: One entry only
entry_id.description: Leave empty to apply to every start/end sensor

prune_datasource.name: Trim a data source to the routes in use
prune_datasource.description: Removes the timetables of routes no sensor reads, then reclaims the space. Routes stay listed, so the config flow still shows them all. Run update_gtfs to restore the full feed.

file.name: Data source
file.description: The sources to prune, picked as devices; plain datasource names still work from yaml. Leave empty to prune every known source; one a train or local stops sensor needs whole is skipped and says so in the response.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: Report what would be removed, without changing anything

intern_datasource.name: Shrink a data source
intern_datasource.description: Replaces the long identifiers repeated on every row by short keys. Run it after trimming. Not reversible in place: run update_gtfs to rebuild from the local zip.

file.name: Data source
file.description: The sources to shrink, picked as devices; plain datasource names still work from yaml. Leave empty to shrink every known source.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: Report what would change, without changing anything

notification.extract_ready:
The source holds **{routes}** lines and **{stops}** stops.

Settings > Devices & services > GTFS2 > Add entry, then **Add a journey between two stops** to carry on.
notification.extract_failed:
The datasource is not usable: {detail}.

Nothing was added. Settings > Devices & services > GTFS2 > Add entry, then **Add a data source** to try again.
notification.import_done:
Brought back into {file}: {lines}.

Settings > Devices & services > GTFS2 > Add entry, then **Add a journey between two stops** to carry on.
notification.import_failed:
The lines could not be brought back into {file}.

Nothing was changed. Settings > Devices & services > GTFS2 > Add entry to try again.
notification.line_orphaned_title: GTFS: {file} keeps a line nobody reads
notification.line_orphaned:
The last sensor reading line **{line}** was removed, but its timetable is still in {file}.

The service gtfs2.prune_datasource drops every line no sensor reads; call it with dry_run first to see what would go. Keeping the line only costs disk space, and adding a sensor on it uses it again.
notification.reason_tables_missing: unpacking stopped before it wrote every table
notification.source_update_available:
The source published a new timetable feed ({version}).

Install it from the **Static feed** update entity of {file}, or let your automation do it. The current data keeps serving until the install swaps it in, in one go.
